sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: Fundamental building blocks of matter: **Atoms** (smallest indivisible unit of an element) and **Molecules** (groups of two or more atoms chemically bonded).
Historical evolution spans from **500 BCE** (Maharishi Kanad / Democritus) to **1808** (Dalton's Atomic Theory) and **1897-1932** (Discovery of subatomic particles).
Applicable across all **chemistry, physics, material science**, and foundational to understanding **General Science** in competitive examinations.
Key contributors include **Maharishi Kanad**, **Democritus**, **John Dalton**, **J.J. Thomson**, **Ernest Rutherford**, **Niels Bohr**, and **Amedeo Avogadro**.
Forms the bedrock of **chemical bonding**, **stoichiometry**, **mole concept**, and **periodic table** behavior evaluated in UPSSSC PET.
**Atomic Structure** (Protons, Neutrons, Electrons), **Atomic Number (Z)**, **Mass Number (A)**, **Isotopes**, **Isobars**, and **Valency**.
High-scoring direct questions on atomic models, discoveries of subatomic particles, chemical laws, and molecular masses appear in every shift.
**Law of Conservation of Mass** (Antoine Lavoisier) and **Law of Constant Proportions** (Joseph Proust).

items.title: 1. Fundamental Particles and Discoveries
items.content:
• **Electron ($e^-$):** Discovered by **J.J. Thomson** (**1897**) using cathode ray tube; charge is **$-1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$**, mass is **$9.1 \times 10^{-31} \text{ kg}$**.
• **Proton ($p^+$):** Discovered by **Eugen Goldstein** (canal rays) and named by **Ernest Rutherford** (**1919**); charge is **$+1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$**, mass is **$1.672 \times 10^{-27} \text{ kg}$**.
• **Neutron ($n^0$):** Discovered by **James Chadwick** (**1932**); neutral charge, mass is approximately **$1.675 \times 10^{-27} \text{ kg}$**.
• **Mnemonic for Subatomic Particles:** **P**en **N**ic **E**raser -> **P**roton = **N**itrogen/Neutron/Names? Better use **P**roton = **R**utherford/Goldstein, **E**lectron = **T**homson, **N**eutron = **C**hadwick -> **PEN** = **P**roton(**E**rnest/Goldstein), **E**lectron(**T**homson), **N**eutron(**C**hadwick). Or use **EPN = T-C-R** (Electron-Thomson, Proton-Rutherford, Neutron-Chadwick).

items.title: 2. Atomic Models Evolution
items.content:
• **Thomson's Plum Pudding Model (1904):** Atom is a positively charged sphere with embedded electrons like plums in pudding or seeds in watermelon.
• **Rutherford's Nuclear Model (1911):** **Alpha-particle scattering experiment** using gold foil; proved presence of a dense, positive **nucleus** and empty space.
• **Bohr's Atomic Model (1913):** Electrons revolve in fixed circular orbits called **stationary states** or **shells (K, L, M, N)** with fixed energy levels.
• **Quantum Mechanical Model:** Modern view treating electrons as waves and particles (**de Broglie**, **Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle**).

items.title: 3. Atomic Number, Mass Number, Isotopes, and Isobars
items.content:
• **Atomic Number ($Z$):** Total number of **protons** in the nucleus of an atom; equals number of electrons in a neutral atom.
• **Mass Number ($A$):** Sum of **protons ($p$) + neutrons ($n$)** in the nucleus ($A = Z + n$).
• **Isotopes:** Atoms of the **same element** having the same atomic number ($Z$) but **different mass numbers** ($A$) due to varying neutrons (e.g., **Protium, Deuterium, Tritium** for Hydrogen).
• **Isobars:** Atoms of **different elements** having the **same mass number** ($A$) but different atomic numbers ($Z$) (e.g., **$_1^3\text{H}$ and $_2^3\text{He}$** or **$_{18}^{40}\text{Ar}$ and $_{20}^{40}\text{Ca}$**).
• **Isotones:** Atoms having the **same number of neutrons** (e.g., $_{6}^{14}	ext{C}$ and $_{8}^{16}	ext{O}$ -> neutrons = $14-6=8$ and $16-8=8$).
• **Isoelectronics:** Species having the **same number of electrons** (e.g., $	ext{O}^{2-}$, $	ext{F}^-$, $	ext{Na}^+$ all have **10 electrons**).

items.title: 4. The Mole Concept and Avogadro's Number
items.content:
• **Mole ($mol$):** Amount of substance that contains as many entities as there are atoms in exactly **$12 \text{ g}$ of Carbon-12** ($^{12}	ext{C}$).;
• **Avogadro Constant ($N_A$):** **$6.022 \times 10^{23}$** particles (atoms, molecules, or ions) per mole.
• **Molar Mass:** Mass of **one mole** of a substance in grams, numerically equal to atomic/molecular mass in atomic mass units (**amu** or **u**).
• **Formulas:** $\text{Moles } (n) = \frac{\text{Given Mass}}{\text{Molar Mass}}$ and $\text{Number of Particles} = n \times N_A$.

items.title: 5. Chemical Bonding and Compounds
items.content:
• **Ionic Bond (Electrovalent):** Formed by complete **transfer of electrons** between a metal and a non-metal (e.g., **$	ext{NaCl}$**).
• **Covalent Bond:** Formed by **sharing of electron pairs** between non-metals (e.g., **$	ext{H}_2$**, **$	ext{O}_2$**, **$	ext{H}_2	ext{O}$**).
• **Coordinate (Dative) Bond:** Shared pair of electrons is contributed by **only one** of the participating atoms.
• **Element vs Compound:** Element consists of identical atoms; compound consists of two or more elements combined in a **fixed mass ratio**.

items.definition: Remember **P-E-N = T-C-R** or **P**roton = **R**utherford/Goldstein, **E**lectron = **T**homson, **N**eutron = **C**hadwick. Another popular mnemonic: **E**ight **P**eople **N**ever **T**alk **C**heats -> **E**lectron = **T**homson, **P**roton = **R**utherford (or Goldstein), **N**eutron = **C**hadwick.
Remember **'C-L-C-P'** -> **C**onservation of mass = **L**avoisier; **C**onstant proportion = **P**roust. Think: 'Lavoisier conserved mass like a pro, Proust proportioned constants nicely'.

items.term: Trick 3: Isotopes vs Isobars Memory Hook
items.definition: Focus on the last letter: Isotop**e**s have same Atomic numb**e**r (Z), Isobar**s** have same Mas**s** number (A). Alternatively: Iso**topes** -> 'p' stands for **Protons/Atomic Number** equal; Iso**bars** -> 'b' stands for **Big mass (Mass number)** equal.

items.term: Trick 4: Valency Rule for Main Group Elements
items.definition: Remember **1-2-3-4-3-2-1-0** rule for valence electrons 1 to 8 in groups 1 to 18. If valence electrons are 1, 2, 3, 4 -> valency is 1, 2, 3, 4. If valence electrons are 5, 6, 7, 8 -> valency is $8-5=3$, $8-6=2$, $8-7=1$, $8-8=0$.
Remember **$6.022 \times 10^{23}$**. Link it mentally: 'Six-O-Double-Two is Avogadro's crew!' Essential for quick mole calculations.
Maximum electrons in any shell = **$2n^2$** where $n$ is shell number ($K=1, L=2, M=3, N=4$). Shell K = $2(1)^2 = 2$; Shell L = $2(2)^2 = 8$; Shell M = $2(3)^2 = 18$; Shell N = $2(4)^2 = 32$.

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing Atomic Number and Mass Number
items.definition: Students often swap $Z$ and $A$ in formulas. Remember: Atomic number ($Z$) is just **protons**; Mass number ($A$) is **protons + neutrons**.

items.term: Mistake 2: Assuming Atoms are Indivisible in Modern Chemistry
items.definition: Dalton stated atoms are indivisible, but modern chemistry proves atoms are divisible into **electrons, protons, and neutrons**.

items.term: Mistake 3: Confusing Isotopes and Isobars Definition
items.definition: Isotopes have same atomic number but different mass numbers (e.g., Hydrogen isotopes). Isobars have different atomic numbers but same mass number (e.g., Argon and Calcium).

items.term: Mistake 4: Miscalculating Molar Mass of Molecules
items.definition: For molecules like $	ext{H}_2	ext{SO}_4$, students forget to multiply atomic masses by the subscript numbers ($2 \times 1 + 32 + 4 \times 16 = 98 \text{ g/mol}$).

items.term: Mistake 5: Confusing Valency with Valence Electrons
items.definition: Valence electrons are electrons in the outermost shell, whereas valency is the combining capacity. For chlorine, valence electrons = 7, but valency = $8-7 = 1$.
Gases like Hydrogen ($	ext{H}_2$), Oxygen ($	ext{O}_2$), Nitrogen ($	ext{N}_2$), and Halogens exist as **diatomic molecules**, not single atoms, under normal conditions.
An **atom** is the smallest particle of an element that takes part in chemical reactions.
A **molecule** is an aggregate of two or more atoms chemically bonded together, representing the smallest unit of a compound.
**John Dalton** proposed the first scientific atomic theory in **1808**, stating matter consists of indivisible atoms.
Atoms consist of **electrons** (negative), **protons** (positive), and **neutrons** (neutral).
Total mass of reactants equals total mass of products in any chemical reaction, given by **Antoine Lavoisier**.
A chemical compound always consists of the same elements combined in the same fixed proportion by mass, given by **Joseph Proust**.
**Atomic number** equals the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.
**Mass number** equals the total sum of protons and neutrons (nucleons) in the nucleus.
**Isotopes** have the same atomic number but different mass numbers due to differing neutron counts.
**Isobars** have different atomic numbers but the exact same mass number.
One mole contains **$6.022 \times 10^{23}$** particles (**Avogadro's Number**).
**Molar mass** is the mass of one mole of a substance expressed in grams per mole ($	ext{g/mol}$).
Atoms combine via **ionic bonds** (electron transfer) or **covalent bonds** (electron sharing) to achieve stable electronic configurations.
**Valency** determines how many bonds an atom can form based on its valence shell electrons.

upscNotes.content: In UPSSSC PET General Science, direct questions are frequently asked from the discoverers of electrons, protons, and neutrons. Memorize the 'PEN-TC' trick thoroughly.

Practice calculating molecular masses for common compounds like $	ext{H}_2	ext{O}$, $	ext{CO}_2$, $	ext{CaCO}_3$, and $	ext{H}_2	ext{SO}_4$ as numerical or direct formula weight questions appear in the exam.

UPSSSC PET examiners often trap students by interchanging the definitions of isotopes and isotones. Always check if the question refers to same atomic number (isotopes) or same number of neutrons (isotones).
Do not confuse valence electrons with valency. For elements with 5, 6, or 7 valence electrons, valency is calculated as $8 - \text{valence electrons}$, not the valence electron number itself.
Remember that Avogadro's number ($6.022 \times 10^{23}$) applies to atoms, molecules, and ions alike. Dimensional analysis using moles is a quick scoring area.

keyTakeaways: Atoms are composed of electrons, protons, and neutrons discovered respectively by J.J. Thomson, Rutherford/Goldstein, and James Chadwick.
Atomic number ($Z$) = number of protons; Mass number ($A$) = protons + neutrons.
Isotopes have identical atomic numbers but different mass numbers; Isobars have identical mass numbers but different atomic numbers.
One mole of any substance contains exactly $6.022 \times 10^{23}$ elementary entities (Avogadro's Number).
Law of Conservation of Mass was given by Lavoisier, and Law of Constant Proportions by Proust.
Chemical bonding occurs through electron transfer (ionic) or electron sharing (covalent) to attain octet stability.
Valency dictates the combining capacity of an element and forms the foundation for writing correct chemical formulas in exam questions.
